newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BOURSE SETS RULES FOR WARRANTS TRADE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BOURSE SETS RULES FOR WARRANTS TRADE.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange approved a set of rules paving the way for trade in warrants on shares, bonds, stock indices and exchange and interest rates, the bourse's deputy president said on Thursday.

Ryszard Czerniawski told a news briefing that under the rules approved by the exchange's supervisory board the bourse would trade in warrants on shares or bonds issued by companies included in the WIG20 blue-chip index at the date of the issue.
The bourse said in a statement the minimum size of the warrant issue would be 10,000 and their expiry period should not be shorter than three months.
The minium value of the underlying bonds or shares was set at three million zlotys.
